exploration.title: Circuit City
exploration.subject: Physics
exploration.summary: Connect three model houses in series or parallel and investigate what happens when a switch opens.
exploration.question: Can one house switch off while the others keep their lights on?
exploration.explanation: Electric current needs a complete path. In a series circuit, the same current passes through every house, so one open switch breaks the whole path. Parallel branches provide separate paths across the battery; opening one branch leaves the others connected. The battery supplies energy, while charge keeps moving around complete paths. These houses are identical, fixed resistances with ideal wires and a battery that never runs down, not a model of household mains wiring.

experiments.title: Break one path
experiments.instruction: Close all three switches in series. Predict which houses lose power when one switch opens, then try it. Repeat in parallel.
experiments.observe: Compare the lit houses and current readings. Explain why one open switch affects every house in series but only its branch in parallel.

experiments.title: Raise the voltage
experiments.instruction: Close all switches and keep the circuit arrangement fixed. Predict the change in current when battery voltage increases, then compare two settings.
experiments.observe: Higher voltage produces more current through the same resistance. Explain why this comparison would change if the resistance also changed.

exploration.misconception: A house uses electrical energy, not a supply of charge that disappears. Current is the rate at which charge passes a point.
